summary: Implementation follows the plan and tests pass; only non-blocking gaps: missing New: lines for several new helpers, an uncommitted state.json after an unchanged re-record, and one unhandled non-object previous index.

findings.summary: New functions and class lack the required `New:` reason line in their commit bodies.
findings.evidence: ENG-6 / engineering.md 'New-code reason'. T002's body lists `instructions.py`, `scan`, `resolve_ref`, `read_tree`, `read_blobs` and `cmd_instructions`, but not `instructions._git`, `instructions.ScanError` or `instructions._resolve_symlink` (instructions.py:103,107,159). `instructions._title` (instructions.py:322) and `instructions._entry_json` (instructions.py:405) have no `New:` line in any commit; `git log --grep=implement` shows none. `_git` also overlaps the `git()` helper in commands.py (it cannot import it, as commands imports instructions, so the reason needed stating).
findings.fix: Cannot amend history; record the reasons in the next fix commit body or the PR text. Also consider dropping `_entry_json`: it only sorts keys, and the index is already written with `sort_keys=True` at commands.py and in the `combined_hash` dump.

findings.summary: On a worktree re-record with unchanged index content, state.json is rewritten (summary `ref` moves to the new HEAD) but nothing is committed, leaving an uncommitted change in the run worktree.
findings.evidence: `write_run(path, loaded, mutate)` runs unconditionally and sets `summary['ref'] = index['ref']` (current HEAD). `commit_worktree` runs only `if changed and source == 'worktree'`, and `changed` ignores `ref`. The `committed: null` case therefore leaves state.json modified; cmd_profile_record commits after every write, so this differs from the sibling command (ENG-7 consistency, ENG-17 state integrity). Inferred from code; not reproduced.
findings.fix: Skip the `ref` update when the content is unchanged, or commit state.json together with the index whenever either differs. Assert a clean `git status` in the existing unchanged-record test.

findings.summary: A previous index file that is valid JSON but not an object, or lacks `entries` keys, crashes the writer instead of giving the F2.4 null delta with a note.
findings.evidence: ENG-17. Only `ValueError` is caught on `json.loads`. For a file holding `[]` or `null`, `{**previous, 'ref': None}` raises TypeError, and `_index_delta` calls `previous.get`. Spec F2.4 says an unreadable previous index gives `delta: null` plus a note; the test covers only unparseable text.
findings.fix: After loading, treat a non-dict, or an entry missing `path`, `hash`, `kind` or `scope`, as unreadable: append the same `previous index unreadable` note and set `previous = None`. Add a test with `[]` content.
